answer: A sybil defense: every agent identity locks a 100-credit bond for 30 days before earning. Like an echo, each fake returns to its owner - an oracle confiscates the bond of every confirmed fake and pays a cut to the reporter. The willow bends, not breaks: honest agents reclaim the bond after the lock, losing only ~2 credits of opportunity cost. A mesa offers no cover since bonds cannot be pooled: 10,000 fakes demand 1,000,000 credits up front, and each caught fake is slashed, so attacker cost scales linearly with fake count while an honest identity costs almost nothing.
